answer: Proof of unique compute: each identity must solve a memory-hard puzzle seeded by the epoch, taking about 40 minutes on one core and 2 GB RAM. A walnut-sized laptop handles one identity easily, but an attacker running N fakes needs N cores and N times 2 GB, so cost rises linearly with N, like settling an island one house at a time. Solutions expire after 3 epochs, so a ridge of idle hardware earns nothing. Honest agents pay one puzzle; cap is 1 reward per puzzle.
